summary: Reproduced the reported NameError in the checked-out entrypoint when ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM is false, then fixed it by importing deep_gemm locally in the independently gated HC-prenorm wrapper after its empty-input fast path. Added regression coverage for forwarding a nonempty call, preserving the empty-input path without DeepGEMM, and reporting ImportError when the dependency is missing.

tests.what_was_measured: The real entrypoint module with ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=false: both nonempty cases failed at entrypoint.py with NameError, while the empty-input boundary passed. Raw output: reports/j-e2a54d63d2f2/raw/failing-before.log
After the fix, all three focused import/control-flow regression cases passed. Raw output: reports/j-e2a54d63d2f2/raw/passing-after.log
Pytest collection and execution passed all three registered CPU tests. Raw output: reports/j-e2a54d63d2f2/raw/pytest-after.log
Formatting, lint, AST, test-registry, and applicable repository hooks passed. Raw output: reports/j-e2a54d63d2f2/raw/pre-commit.log
The patch contains no whitespace errors. Raw output: reports/j-e2a54d63d2f2/raw/git-diff-check.log

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned device is an AMD Instinct MI355X with gfx950 under ROCm 7.2. The reported kernel is a CUDA DeepGEMM TF32 path on H100/SM90, so no GPU kernel or DeepSeek-V4 forward execution was claimed. Device probe: reports/j-e2a54d63d2f2/raw/gpu-environment.log

remaining_limitations: DeepSeek-V4 weights were not available, so the full model serving/forward path was not run.
The assigned gfx950 ROCm GPU cannot validate the reported CUDA DeepGEMM TF32 kernel on H100/SM90.
The regression validates the actual Python wrapper's import gating and call forwarding with a stub kernel; it does not validate kernel numerical accuracy or model semantics.
